variables.name: study_title
variables.description: Compose a descriptive study title from the context, not a copy of any section heading. Work in whichever of these the study actually has: test article identity, test system/species, nature of the study (e.g. pharmacodynamic, pharmacokinetic, toxicology), route of administration, dose or duration. Title case throughout. Example shape only, not a template to fill in verbatim: 'An 8-Week Repeat Dose Study Evaluating Plasma PAL and Phenylalanine Levels in Male ENU2 Mice Following 3x Weekly Subcutaneous Administration of 45kD POEGMA-PAL (BMN 390)'. Primarily sourced from the Cayuse protocol.

variables.name: study_number
variables.description: Extract the Study Number from the context. It usually starts with ARN-XX-XXX followed by numbers. Primarily sourced from the Cayuse protocol.

variables.name: study_summary
variables.description: Extract the study summary along with proposed experiments. Return the full text exactly as written, preserving original wording and formatting. Primarily sourced from the Cayuse protocol.

variables.name: study_objective
variables.description: Summarize the study objective. Primarily sourced from the Cayuse protocol.

variables.name: justification_for_species_selection
variables.description: Extract the justification for species selection. State a justification only if the protocol itself gives one, or if the species/strain choice is unusual enough to need scientific explaining (e.g. not a standard laboratory strain for this kind of study) -- don't fabricate a justification for a routine choice the protocol doesn't explain. Primarily sourced from the Cayuse protocol.

variables.name: dose_administration
variables.description: Extract dose administration of test article details from Route of Administration, Dose and Volume of Administration, Site and Frequency of Administration sections.

variables.name: day_of_first_dose
variables.description: Extract the day of first dose.

variables.name: last_day_of_necropsy
variables.description: Extract the last day of necropsy.

call_groups.name: experimental_articles
call_groups.description: Before answering any field below, resolve the study's own design once: which article is under test, and which arm is the actual comparator. The comparator may be the vehicle itself -- treat any 'ignore the vehicle' framing as conditional on a distinct, named non-vehicle control article actually existing (e.g. an older-generation drug in a studies comparing generations); if the vehicle alone is what the test article is compared against, the vehicle is the control article. Certificates of Testing and formulation/dosing-request records often refer to the same test or control article by an internal formulation code rather than the protocol's article name -- match these by dose level and chemical description before concluding a source doesn't cover that article. A vehicle's own characterization (its lot, expiration, manufacturer, storage) may be recorded separately from the test article's -- e.g. in its own formulation or component-supplier records -- rather than left out entirely; check for those before returning not_found on a vehicle-as-control field. Answer every field below consistently against this resolution, not re-derived per field.

variables.name: test_and_control_article_characterization
variables.description: Extract how test and control articles are characterized.

variables.name: dose_preparation_and_analysis_for_test_or_control_articles
variables.description: Extract dose preparation and analysis details for test or control articles.

variables.name: number_of_study_groups
variables.description: Extract the number of study groups. Count different doses as different study groups.

variables.name: test_article_name
variables.description: Extract the test article's name, including different concentrations used for the same article, if any.

variables.name: test_article_description
variables.description: Extract the test article's description.

variables.name: test_article_lot_number
variables.description: Extract the test article's lot number(s).

variables.name: test_article_expiration_date
variables.description: Extract the test article's expiration date.

variables.name: test_article_manufacturer_supplier
variables.description: Extract the test article's manufacturer/supplier.

variables.name: test_article_storage
variables.description: Extract the test article's storage information.

variables.name: control_article_name
variables.description: Extract the control article's name, including different concentrations used for the same article, if any.

variables.name: control_article_lot_number
variables.description: Extract the control article's lot number(s).

variables.name: control_article_expiration_date
variables.description: Extract the control article's expiration date.

variables.name: control_article_manufacturer_supplier
variables.description: Extract the control article's manufacturer/supplier.

variables.name: control_article_storage
variables.description: Extract the control article's storage information.

variables.name: animal_species
variables.description: Extract the animal species used in this study and return the species name exactly as written.

variables.name: animal_strains
variables.description: Extract the animal strains used in this study and return the strain name exactly as written.

variables.name: animal_supplier
variables.description: Extract the animal supplier used in this study and return the supplier name, city, state, country exactly as written.

variables.name: total_number_of_animals
variables.description: Extract the total number of animals used in the study and include sex counts when available. Output format: '<total> (male: <number_of_males>, female: <number_of_females>)'. If only one sex count is explicitly provided and total is known, infer the missing sex as remainder: missing = total - provided_count. Use '<total> (gender not specified)' only when no sex-specific counts are available.

variables.name: animal_identification
variables.description: Extract the method used to identify animals/organisms in detail (e.g., Tag, Tattoo).

variables.name: age_of_dosing
variables.description: ONLY extract the age at dosing.

variables.name: animal_weight_at_dosing
variables.description: ONLY extract the target weight at dosing with units.

variables.name: environmental_acclimation
variables.description: Extract the environmental acclimation period or process (You MUST only give me the time value (number of days or weeks), no prose).

variables.name: housing_environment_conditions
variables.description: Extract housing and environmental conditions from the protocol's own housing/environment section: caging and bedding, diet standard, room temperature/humidity/light-cycle controls, animal room occupancy, and cage labeling practice. Write it as one prose paragraph in past tense, using the protocol's own stated values where given; fall back to standard IACUC-facility conventions only for whatever the protocol itself leaves unstated. Style reference only, not a fill-in template: 'Animals were housed in Makrolon cages with microisolator caps, using contact bedding, and provided with free access to a standard rodent chow which meets the requirements of the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.'

variables.name: food_and_water_provided
variables.description: Extract all available details about the food and water provided to animals. Convert to past tense.

variables.name: additional_animal_information
variables.description: Summarize relevant details about the spare animals used in this study. Include species, strain, source/vendor, identification method, health status/quarantine, housing and enrichment, age and weight at dosing, and other notable animal-related information as a brief 1-2 paragraph summary.

variables.name: methods_of_euthanasia
variables.description: Extract information about the methods of euthanasia used for Animals euthanized before scheduled termination and for Animals euthanized at scheduled termination. Include details about the method, agent, and any relevant notes.

variables.name: deaths_and_unscheduled_euthanasia
variables.description: Extract a summary of procedures from Veterinary Care section for deaths and unscheduled euthanasia, including who determines unscheduled euthanasia, methods used, and necropsy type. Provide a concise paragraph.

variables.name: scheduled_euthanasia_and_necropsy
variables.description: Extract a summary of procedures for scheduled euthanasia and necropsy, including timing, methods, and necropsy procedures. Provide a concise paragraph.

variables.name: experimental_design
variables.description: Summarize the experimental design from the section labeled 'Experimental Information'. Preserve original wording, without the section heading. DO NOT include the experimental design table.

variables.name: experimental_design_table
variables.description: Extract the experimental design table. Understand the table structure and information conveyed and sanitize the table to include correct information under the correct column names. If values appear shifted into neighboring cells, correct the placement using header meaning, row context, data type patterns, and consistency with nearby rows.

variables.name: justification_for_dosage_selection
variables.description: Extract the full text that provides justification for dose selection and route of administration, including dose concentration, compound names, endotoxin levels, vehicle control, route, and calculation notes. Preserve original wording.

variables.name: terminal_sample_collection
variables.description: Extract a summary of when and how terminal samples were collected for each sample type, specifying timing, procedures used, sample types, and processing or storage details.

variables.name: timepoints_when_animals_observed
variables.description: Summarize in brief the timepoints when animals were observed from the given table.

variables.name: timepoints_when_body_weights_measured
variables.description: Summarize in brief the timepoints when body weights were measured from the given table.

variables.name: in_life_procedures
variables.description: Extract other in-life procedures, measures, observations taken. If available, also add key efficacy endpoints first then secondary efficacy endpoints, each introduced with a plain-text label (e.g. 'Key efficacy endpoints: ...') rather than a heading.

variables.name: in_life_sample_collections
variables.description: Extract details on when and how samples were collected for each sample type from the given table.

variables.name: in_life_sample_analysis
variables.description: Extract all the sample analysis details from the given table.

variables.name: tissue_collection_organ_weights_table
variables.description: Extract tissue collection organ weights table table but only include the tissues relevant to this study.

variables.name: tissue_preservation_details
variables.description: Extract the tissue preservation details.

variables.name: deviations_table
variables.description: Extract the procedures where deviations were made, and make a table with procedure as one column and deviation details as another column.

variables.name: study_director
variables.description: Extract the Study Director name.

variables.name: report_author
variables.description: Extract the Report Author name and other details if present.

variables.name: principal_investigator
variables.description:
Extract the Principal Investigator (sometimes named PI in the protocol) name and other details if present. Format: Name: <name> 
 Phone: <phone> 
 Email: <email>.

variables.name: additional_study_personnel
variables.description: Extract ALL additional study personnel / research staff members.

variables.name: research_project_lead
variables.description: Extract the Research Project Lead name and other details if present.

variables.name: ta_head
variables.description: Extract the TA (Therapeutic Area) Head or equivalent management sign-off name and other details if present.

call_groups.name: results
call_groups.description: This study's actual measured outcome (e.g. an expression or biomarker readout) often lives only in chart or plot images attached under a Benchling entry's own results-style heading (e.g. 'Results', 'Data', 'Analysis'), with little or no describing text alongside them. Before treating a results field as not_found or methods-only, check for that shape -- a heading followed by images and thin text -- and inspect_image those images; the finding is usually in the image, not the surrounding prose.

variables.name: executive_summary_of_key_results
variables.description: Summarize the key results of the study in brief.

variables.name: in_life_procedures_key_results
variables.description: Add key results for all in-life procedures including: animal mortality/morbidity, observations, body weights, other procedures. Include animal body weights (individual and mean/SD) over the duration of the study and give a brief written description.

variables.name: dose_analysis_key_results
variables.description: Extract all key results for dose analysis in this study.

variables.name: all_other_results
variables.description: Extract all results for this study, excluding results for dose analysis and in-life procedures.

call_groups.name: conclusions
call_groups.description: Base every field below only on the Benchling experimental results -- including attached files, and images inspected via inspect_image where a results section is image-only. Use the Cayuse protocol only to understand the study's objective and design, never as a source of findings; do not reach for it to fill a gap in Benchling's results. If, after checking both text and images, Benchling doesn't contain enough result data to support a conclusion, say so plainly rather than forcing one.

variables.name: study_conclusions_brief_summary
variables.description: Capture the overarching findings relevant to the study objective in 2-3 concise sentences, because it's a brief summary.

variables.name: study_conclusions
variables.description: Capture the overarching findings relevant to the study objective, as a paragraph or as separate plain sentences, one per line, not a Markdown bullet list.

variables.name: discussion_and_interpretation
variables.description: Discuss the significance and implications of the findings relevant to the study objective.
